claims.text: A mixed economic system is an economic system in which resources are allocated partly by market forces acting through prices and private firms, and partly by government through its budget, its public services and the firms it owns.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A market economic system leaves allocation to private owners responding to prices, a command system places allocation with a central authority, and a mixed system combines elements of the two, with the balance drawn differently in different countries.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: In a mixed economic system the private sector tends to produce everyday goods and services for markets, while government provides state services such as schools and hospitals, builds infrastructure, owns a share of firms and steps in where it judges a market outcome to be failing.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Namibia and Germany both run mixed economies: private firms trade through markets in each, while the state funds schools and hospitals, runs railways and sets rules, with the weighting between market and state differing between the two countries.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Government intervention to address market failure is deliberate action by a government to change the outcome a market reaches on its own, taken because the outcome is judged to waste resources or to leave needs unmet.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A maximum price held below the market price tends to make the quantity demanded exceed the quantity supplied, creating a shortage, while a minimum price held above the market price tends to make the quantity supplied exceed the quantity demanded, creating a surplus.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An indirect tax raises the cost of supplying a good, which tends to raise its market price and reduce the quantity traded, while a subsidy lowers the cost of supplying a good, which tends to reduce its market price and raise the quantity traded.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A government can also intervene through regulation, which sets binding rules producers must follow; direct provision, in which the government supplies the good itself; privatisation, which moves a state-owned firm into private hands; and nationalisation, which moves a private firm into state ownership.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
